headline: Carry the count of every reachable signed sum
statement: Assign a plus or minus sign independently to every element in nums. Return how many sign assignments evaluate to target. Equal values and zeros still occupy separate positions.
intuition: Choose a plus or minus sign for each number. Different sign choices may give the same total, so save a count for each possible total. For the next number, send each old count to both the plus total and the minus total in a new map.
approach: Reject abs(target)>sum(nums) or incompatible parity before building states.
Begin with one way to make zero using no numbers.
For every number, build a fresh map by sending each old count to sum+value and sum-value.
Read the final count for target, defaulting to zero.
correctness: Each assignment of the first i numbers extends uniquely with a plus or minus choice for number i+1. The two updates accumulate all such extensions, including different choices producing the same sum. Induction gives exact counts after the final number.
bruteForce: List all 2^n sign assignments and compute each sum; this does not merge identical intermediate sums.

complexity.explanation: S is sum(nums). At most 2S+1 signed sums occur, including one sum for an all-zero input; only two maps are retained.

pitfalls: Use a fresh map each round to avoid consuming a number repeatedly.
